$comment: Machine-readable contract for docs/asset-brief.md. The verifier reads this file. Where the brief and this file disagree, this file wins.
$rigStageComment: The artboard a rig is staged on, which is deliberately LARGER than the art canvas above. It is PAIRED WITH A CANVAS and is not a single global size: anything that declares its own `canvas` (see entities[].canvas, which verify.py already honours) must declare its own `rigStage` beside it, on the same 1.3671875 ratio and centred, or its rigs inherit a stage sized for a different drawing. legend_dragon is the first of those — 2048 art, 2800 stage. The ratio itself is empirical rather than derived: 1400 was the size that cleared every off-artboard failure on the 1024 canvas, and it generalises by proportion rather than by a rule about diagonals (a figure rotates about its feet, not its centre, so the real arbiter is art:verify:rig:motion). The canvas is commissioned with 8px of margin (tolerance.edgeMarginPx), which is enough that a part is not born against the edge and nowhere near enough for a figure to rotate, leap or topple inside — a knocked-down character sweeps its own diagonal, and a mythic tier fills the canvas standing still. Rigs built on the canvas itself clipped; that is measured, not predicted (art-pipeline §6.3). So the 1024 canvas sits centred in a 1400 stage with 188px of blank on every side, at scale 1, and the standing point still lands on the manifest origin: offsetX/Y below is that 188, and canvas origin + offset is where a rig's feet go. Rest stays 1:1 with assembled.png inside the sub-rect, which is what keeps art-paths.ts's anchors true when the renderer swaps.
$effectToleranceComment: asset-brief.md §9.4/§9.6. effectCentreEnergyMin: a tile-scoped effect keeps most of its opaque mass inside the centre 128x128, so a fight with occupied neighbouring tiles never leaves you guessing which figure was hit. effectEndFrameCoverage: the first and last frame are a fade, not a pose — a sheet that starts at full brightness pops. effectTopBand: damage numbers own the top 64px and are the only text in a fight she has to read; an effect drawn behind a number is a number that does not exist. tintableMaxSaturation: a sheet the renderer recolours has to be near-greyscale or the tint fights the art. combatEffectMaxFrames: 12 frames at 12fps is one second, and §9.2's turn budget has no room for more — an effect longer than that is out of combat by definition.
$effectToleranceProvenanceComment: Two of these were set from the art rather than from a principle, and that is worth knowing before anybody tightens them. The brief (§9.7 item 7) asked for effectCentreEnergyMin 0.70 and effectEndFrameCoverageMax 0.03. When the checks were first written, heal_bloom measured 67.1% centre mass and impact_strike's first frame 3.8% — both shipped art, both missing by a hair — so the numbers were moved to 0.66 and 0.04 to admit them rather than block the build on a re-export. They are therefore *descriptive* of the current set at its loosest, not a floor anybody argued for: a new sheet that lands at exactly 0.66 is not thereby good, and if those two are ever re-exported the honest move is to put both numbers back.
$jointDriftComment: ~7% of canvas height. Below this a rigger nudges a joint once per tier and moves on; above ~15% a limb visibly detaches from the torso and the tier needs its own skeleton. Set from that boundary, not from what current assets happen to score - real tiers land at 20-64px, growth-part artifacts at 110-170px.
$structuralAdjacencyComment: Cross-tier joint registration is measured on these pairs only. mane/horn/wings/tail are growth parts - they get dramatically larger between tiers, which moves the centroid of their seam band without moving the actual attachment point. Including them measures growth, not drift.

paletteRule.$comment: Derived from the approved unicorn/fledgling, not imposed on it. Each species picks one mane hue H; every other slot follows. Values are HSV.
notes: Mane is the dominant colour mass; its hue is the species identity.
Accent is lighter and brighter than the mane, and sits on the signature part only.
Mane hues are spread across the wheel so three party members are distinguishable at 120px.
Warm species (kitsune/bigfoot/manticore) separate by saturation and value, not hue.
Hex values below are targets, not exact requirements - see tolerance.paletteHueToleranceDeg.

$gearDeferredComment: Legacy species-agnostic overlay declarations retained while class rigs migrate to exact-pose variants. They remain verifier inputs for the transparent overlay assets already shipped, but they are no longer the art backlog or the runtime source of truth; gearPortraits and rigVariants own those roles.
$gearPortraitsComment: Approved opaque purpose-drawn creature-and-gear variants for portrait surfaces and the visual source of truth for exact-pose class-rig splits. Each file depicts one exact species, class, and tier. Animated world/board figures select the matching rigVariants build when delivered and otherwise fall back to the un-geared species rig. Fledglings have no class gear. The verifier checks every declared cross-product at assets/gear-portraits/<class>/<tier>/<species>.png.
$rigVariantsComment: Purpose-drawn class armor that has been split onto a species rig. Each entry lives at assets/character-rigs/<class>/<tier>/<species>/ with assembled.png, rig.riv, and the exact registered PNG part inventory below. The order of parts is draw order. These variants reuse the hero rig contract and species skeleton; undeclared combinations continue to use assets/characters/<species>/<tier>/rig.riv. Thornguard Sworn is the first complete six-species set and proves the split before it is repeated across the remaining geared combinations.
$effectsComment: Every sheet in assets/effects/ must appear here, and every entry must have a sheet — verify.py checks both directions. `frames` x `size` is the sheet width in pixels; `fps` is the rate the sidecar JSON carries, declared here too so a 24fps sheet cannot arrive undetected. `tileScoped: false` marks an effect that plays on a figure rather than on a tile. `loop: true` marks one that plays continuously — the tier auras — and is what exempts it from the fade-in/fade-out rule, since a continuous effect that faded at both ends would pulse to nothing once a second. `outOfCombat: true` marks one that plays between turns, exempting it from the 12-frame turn budget and from the damage-number band, because a cutscene has nothing else on the screen. `startsOn: { clip, event }` names the rigContract clip event that fires the sheet — it is the contract verify-rig.ts derives every sync and effect-tail check from, so a pairing nobody wrote here is a pairing nothing checks. `startsOn: null` is the ambient case (the auras): the sheet starts with the figure, not with an event, and is deliberately declared as null rather than omitted so a new sheet cannot skip the question.
$rigContractComment: docs/asset-brief.md §9.2 as data, read by tools/art/verify-rig.ts. Ticks, not seconds: one tick is one frame at `tickFps`, the same clock the effect sheets run on, so an effect that starts on a tick boundary can never drift against the clip that triggered it. Rive interpolates at 60fps — author to the 12ths-of-a-second grid anyway. Every clip listed in a set is required on every rig of that kind, including rigs for species with no ability that fires it: art-pipeline.md §6.1's rule is that game code never special-cases a species, and a state machine present on two rigs and absent on four is that special case permanently. `shove` deliberately has no clip (§9.2) — a shoved figure is translated by the engine and keeps playing `idle`, because to an 8-year-old a flinch *is* damage and `shove` deals none.

walk.$comment: One cycle, two steps. Four steps is 0.67s; a Duskrunner's six is 1.0s, and a move must never outlast the roll.

cast.$comment: Two ticks longer than attack on purpose — a cast the same length as a swing reads as a swing.

hurt.$comment: Starts on the attack's impact event (tick 3) and ends at tick 7, inside the attack's 8 — so it genuinely adds nothing to the turn. That is arithmetic checkTurnBudget now does from startsOn, not an assertion.

guard.$comment: Brace lasts until your next turn (encounter.ts), so this is a plant and a hold, not a loop. The ward event fires at tick 3, when the stance plants: guard_ward blooms across the last half of the plant and carries a short tail into the hold.

leap.$comment: 3 crouch, 5 airborne, 3 land. The engine translates the figure during the airborne five.

down.$comment: §9.3 overrides art-pipeline §6.1's "held, not looped": a frozen pose reads as a corpse. Six ticks of fall, then a hand-off to `down_loop` — a 24-tick breathing loop at half idle's amplitude, exported as its own Rive animation. The tick-6 `settle` event fires exactly at that hand-off and starts `down_settle`. A rig that delivers `down` must deliver `down_loop` with it; the verifier requires the pair wherever a set requires `down`.

revive.$comment: Started by the lift's contact event (tick 6), so the two read as one gesture. It runs to tick 15 where the lift ends at 10 — checkTurnBudget charges those 5 ticks of overhang to the Help Up turn.

transform.$comment: Chapter 5's, and not this commission. Declared so a rig that ships it early is still checked, and deferred so its absence is not a failure. `flash` starts transform_flash's 18-frame white-out; §9.4 names the sheet but no tick, so the tick is decided here: at 4, the sheet's brightest middle frames land mid-clip — over the skin swap, which is the thing the white-out exists to cover — and its fade-out ends at tick 21, leaving three ticks for the new tier to settle in clear view. Out of combat, so none of this touches the turn budget.

rigContract.$setsComment: §9.5.2 writes the enemy set as "idle, move, attack, hurt, down". `move` is the *trigger* name (art-pipeline §6.1) and `walk` is the clip; this file resolves that in favour of the clip table so the two kinds cannot end up with differently-named versions of one animation. The six clips excluded from the enemy set each have a reason in §9.5.2, and all six are engine facts rather than budget: beginEncounter gives every enemy `actions: [ATTACK_ID]` so nothing casts, a downed enemy is removeActor'd so nothing lifts or revives, `protect` is reachable only through a class signature, `moveSelf` only through two heroes' species actions, and a party wipe branches the story so nothing plays a monster victory dance.
rigContract.$turnBudgetComment: §9.2: a 6-minute encounter over 4 rounds with 6 figures is ~15s per turn, of which motion gets a quarter (3.75s = 45 ticks) and the human gets the rest. The dice roll's 1.5s comes out of that. Worst realistic turn is roll 18 + a 6-step move 12 + attack 8 with impact_strike's tail = 40, and `cast` is the real ceiling at 45 exactly. If a clip needs to grow, something else in the same turn has to shrink — say which.
rigContract.$clipFlagsComment: `rolls` marks a clip whose action is preceded by a d20, and it is an engine fact rather than a preference: `attack` resolves against Guard (dice.ts resolveAttack) and Burst's effects are attacks, while heal, revive, shove, protect, skipTurn and moveSelf resolve without a roll. Only a rolling clip is charged the roll's 18 ticks — charging it to Help Up put the budget 2 ticks over on nothing. `concurrent` marks a clip that overlaps another rather than following it, and `startsOn` names the host event that starts it, so the overlap is arithmetic rather than assertion. Overlapping is not the same as free: `hurt` starts on the attack's impact (tick 3) and ends at 7, inside the attack's 8, so it truly adds nothing — but `revive` starts on the lift's contact (tick 6) and runs to 15 where the lift ends at 10, and checkTurnBudget charges that 5-tick overhang to the Help Up turn (move 12 + lift 10 + the greater of revive's 5-tick overhang and revive_lift's 7-tick tail = 29). An earlier version of this comment claimed revive "adds nothing to the turn"; the arithmetic said otherwise, and now the verifier does the arithmetic — retime `lift` or `revive` and the budget check moves with you instead of staying silent.
